Q1 — the plugin's Stop pipeline: hooks/hooks.json Stop entry runs stop-gates.sh through run-hook.py; stop-gates.sh runs the wiring gate unconditionally, then skill-registry, native-contract and genericity gates by scope test over the worktree plus the branch's commits; native-contract runs again from precommit-gates.sh at commit time. Registries read: .claude-plugin/plugin.json skills[]+agents[] (check A), .codex-plugin/plugin.json skills[] (rule C), CLAUDE.md + README.md text (check B), MANIFEST.md E-table (check C), LANGUAGE.md token in SKILL.md/agents (check D), providers/codex/agents/*.toml (rule D), CAPABILITIES.md `Shared hook events/matchers:` lines (rule E), PROVIDERS.md Supported harnesses (rule H), genericity-allow.txt + sensitive-patterns.tsv, .claude/wiring-ious.md.

Q1 — pointer-line contract: LANGUAGE.md:10-15 and CLAUDE.md:48 require every SKILL.md and agent definition to open with a LANGUAGE.md pointer; check D (`grep -L 'LANGUAGE\.md'`) enforces it over skills/afk/*/SKILL.md, skills/utils/*/SKILL.md, agents/*.md only — root doctrine files, sibling .md files and pointer lines to DELEGATION.md / INVESTIGATION.md / DECISIONS.md are convention (LANGUAGE.md's opening paragraph, DECISIONS.md:3, INVESTIGATION.md:7) with no gate. All six caller skills carry the LANGUAGE.md pointer at SKILL.md line 6.

Q1 — where a utility pointer line would land in the six caller skills: grill-requirements `## During the session` claims step (SKILL.md:46, beside the /afk:investigate + INVESTIGATION.md pointer); grill-solution Grilling protocol step 1 (SKILL.md:76); grill-verification Process step 1 (SKILL.md:55); review `What the review reads` item 4 (SKILL.md:38); adversary Process step 1 (SKILL.md:25); fix Phase 1 / Phase 3 (SKILL.md:28, :70). Such a line is plugin prose: native-contract rule A and the genericity gate scan it; no registry or check reads it.

Q2 — what reaches the gates: hooks/hooks.json:59 (Stop) and hooks.codex.json:59 (twin, pinned by hook-smoke.sh:243); precommit-gates.sh:154 (native-contract at commit); /afk:setup audit check 5 runs native-contract-gate.sh standalone (AUDIT.md:70) and checks 1/4/6 re-derive the registry agreement, FRESHNESS rows and glossary usage without a gate; FRESHNESS.md rows 38-66 name the same-commit surfaces; hooks/README.md:62-64,104 document the checks. Tests: only check F (test_skill_frontmatter.py:86), the hooks.json twin (hook-smoke.sh:243) and the genericity cache-key/malformed-pattern paths (hook-smoke.sh:269-324) are pinned; skill-registry checks A-E, every native-contract rule, wiring-gate.sh and stop-gates.sh dispatch have no test (grep over hooks/tests and scripts/tests).

claims.text: Q3 — add a skill directory: same commit = .claude-plugin/plugin.json skills[] (skill-registry check A, hooks/skill-registry-gate.sh:70,107-108 -> exit 2) + .codex-plugin/plugin.json skills[] (native-contract rule C, :188-194) + a /afk:<name>, `<name>` or skills/<family>/<name> mention in BOTH CLAUDE.md and README.md (check B, :124-135) + LANGUAGE.md pointer line in the new SKILL.md (check D, :183) + frontmatter name == directory with allowed keys (check F :203 / skill_frontmatter_check.py:82; rule B :146-162) + prose free of harness vocabulary and ticket ids (rule A :79-134; genericity :156-251). Not gate-enforced: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] (FRESHNESS.md:40), CAPABILITIES.md Skill requirements row when it needs a capability (:44), providers/CONFORMANCE.md skill count (:18). SKILL.md is wiring-exempt (wiring-gate.sh:34); a sibling .md needs a referrer.

Q3 — add an agent file agents/<name>.md: same commit = .claude-plugin/plugin.json agents[] (check A, hooks/skill-registry-gate.sh:74-77,110-111) + providers/codex/agents/afk-<name>.toml (native-contract rule D, :200-203) + LANGUAGE.md pointer line (check D, :183-184) + a referrer token elsewhere or an IOU (wiring-gate.sh: agents/*.md is not conventional at :34, orphan at :199; the plugin.json entry is the referrer) + prose scans (rule A, genericity). .codex-plugin/plugin.json has no agents[] (rule C checks skills only). Not gate-enforced: DELEGATION.md:26 named types + :45 tier, the skills that spawn it (FRESHNESS.md:61), CHANGELOG.md.

Q3 — add a root doctrine file <NAME>.md: no registry check reads it. Gates that touch it: wiring gate (not a conventional name at wiring-gate.sh:34-35 -> needs a referrer token elsewhere, e.g. a CLAUDE.md Reference line, or an IOU; orphan -> exit 2 at :199), native-contract rule A prose scan (:79-134), genericity gate added-line scan (:156). Check D does NOT cover it (only SKILL.md + agents/*.md). Not gate-enforced: CLAUDE.md Reference list (:189-201), README.md root-doc list (:829), a FRESHNESS.md registry row (:56), and pointer lines in the skills that use it (LANGUAGE.md:10-15 convention).

Q3 — add a glossary term (GLOSSARY.md `**Term**:` heading): no Stop gate reads GLOSSARY.md (GLOSSARY.md is wiring-conventional at wiring-gate.sh:34; the added line passes the rule-A and genericity scans unless it names a harness or a ticket id). Only /afk:setup audit check 6 (AUDIT.md:78-80, scripts/glossary_usage.py:110-130) requires >=1 consumer file per term; FRESHNESS.md:44 names the row.

Q3 — add a capability row (CAPABILITIES.md table :7-22 or Skill requirements :37-44): no gate parses the tables; native-contract rule E reads only the `Shared hook events:` / `Shared hook matchers:` lines (:26,28 via native-contract-gate.sh:212-226), and CAPABILITIES.md is excluded from the rule-A prose scan (:78). Registry-only: FRESHNESS.md:62 (CAPABILITIES.md + PROVIDERS.md together); the genericity gate still scans the added line.

Q3 — add a pointer line in a caller skill (e.g. `see X.md` in grill-requirements/grill-solution/grill-verification/review/adversary/fix SKILL.md): gates that see it are native-contract rule A (harness vocabulary, bare PLUGIN_ROOT — write `${AFK_PLUGIN_ROOT}`), genericity (ticket ids, product symbols), and — when the pointed-at file is new — the wiring gate, for which the pointer is the referrer that wires it. No registry, manifest or check D reads the line. /afk:setup audit check 3 (AUDIT.md:40-50) requires the cited path to resolve on disk.

Deployment order / cross-site: every gate-enforced pair is checked inside one Stop turn on the same tree, so the set ships in one commit (FRESHNESS.md:13-18 same-commit rule); the harness loader (B14, frontier) reads plugin.json after /reload-plugins, so an entry pointing at a dir not yet on disk is `stale` (check A :113-117) and a dir without an entry is invisible — no ordering across commits keeps both sides working.
Test coverage of the gate checks that enforce the same-commit set is absent except check F (frontmatter) and the hooks.json twin; a regression in check A/B/D or rules C/D would not fail any suite.
